channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: SoftBank Credit Risk Tops 500 Basis Points as AI Worries Mount
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp.’s credit risk surged above 500 basis points for the first time in about four years, raising the prospect of even higher funding costs as the company presses ahead with massive investments in artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Takahiko Hyuga

item.title: US Chip Curbs Stall Asia Data Center Financing
item.description: US chip curbs are putting the brakes on billions of dollars in AI data center financing across Asia, with lenders reassessing deals tied to Chinese tech firms including ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent. Bloomberg’s Annabelle Droules says legal and compliance risks are weighing on banks as new rules on chip access take effect. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microdramas Rake in $20 Billion as World Gloms On to Quick Hits
item.description: Minutes-long microdramas are set to notch $20 billion in revenue this year as global viewers swarm to their screens in search of quick, easy hits.
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Ng

item.title: Markets Stage a Stunning Reversal Ahead of Thanksgiving
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Yardeni Research President & Chief Investment Strategist Ed Yardeni, Barclays Managing Director, Senior Retail Analyst Adrienne Yih, Baird Senior Research Analyst Mig Dobre, PSP Growth Managing Director & Head of Venture Momei Qu, Westwood CIO of Multi-Asset Strategies Adrian Helfert, LSEG Director of Consumer Research Jharonne Martis, Balsam Hill CEO & Founder Mac Harman, Seven-Time Major Tennis Champion & WeWard Investor Venus Williams, & Pro Shop Co-Founder & President Chad Mumm. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pro Shop’s Chad Mumm on Skins Game Return To Prime Video
item.description: “The Farmers Insurance Skins Game” returns to Prime video this Friday for a second year in a row. This year’s event features PGA tour veterans and rookies vying for chance to win $4 million at the Atlantic Field Clubs in Florida. Chad Mumm, Co-Founder and President of the golf media and commerce company Pro Shop, joined Bloomberg’s Romaine Bostick to discuss the revival of the iconic game and what’s different this year. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Balsam Hill CEO on Christmas Tree Shopping Outlook
item.description: Mac Harman, CEO and Founder of Balsam Hill, says the company saw strong interest early in the season, but some consumers appear to be holding off, possibly until the coming weekend. Customers who shop online are completing purchases. Harman says Balsam Hill serves shoppers across income levels: many save for its lifelike trees, while ornaments and other accessories tend to appeal to more premium buyers. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Still in Early Innings of AI Adoption: PSP’s Momei Qu
item.description: Momei Qu, Managing Director and Head of Venture at PSP Growth, says Anthropic is in a period of price discovery as public-market investors work out how to value a frontier AI company. Compared with SaaS predecessors, Anthropic may offer faster growth and a larger addressable market, but investors are weighing substantial capital expenditure, uncertain long-term margins and questions about its competitive moat. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Financials, Healthcare Will Be Big AI Winners: Yardeni
item.description: Ed Yardeni, President and Chief Investment Strategist at Yardeni Research, described the market’s sharp intraday reversal as another attempt to find a bottom, following recent steep losses and Monday’s dramatic rebound. He pointed to support around 69,077,000 as transcribed, and said dip buyers were stepping in at these levels. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 1Password Says Hacker Accessed User Data, Passwords Remain Safe
item.description: 1Password said a hacker accessed some of its internal systems and obtained a limited amount of account information from users, but the company noted that passwords were not compromised.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Murphy Kelly

item.title: Anthropic’s Stock Sparks Rare Divide Inside One Wall Street Firm
item.description: Two equity analysts at a single Wall Street research firm have taken the unusual step of posting conflicting views on the outlook for the hottest stock in the market: Anthropic PBC’s newly listed shares.
item.dc:creator: Henry Ren

item.title: JPMorgan Sees $450 Billion AI Debt Blitz in 2027 Before Plateau
item.description: Companies will tap public high-grade debt markets for $450 billion next year to finance their artificial intelligence-related capital expenditures, even as a growth plateau looms for the burgeoning industry further down the road, according to analysts at JPMorgan Chase & Co.
item.dc:creator: Zahra Tayeb

item.title: AI Uncertainty Drives Wild Swings, Nasdaq Ends Down 0.6% After Sharp Selloff
item.description: As soon as the opening bell rang on the New York Stock Exchange, the sell orders started pouring in and everybody, it seemed, was again making another jarring rush for the exits.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Menton, Matthew Griffin and Geoffrey Morgan

item.title: Palo Alto Networks Accused by Ex-Manager of Accounting Fraud
item.description: Palo Alto Networks Inc., which last week announced a $4.5 billion AI acquisition, was sued by a former executive over claims he was fired for fighting back against accounting fraud at the cybersecurity company.
item.dc:creator: Chris Dolmetsch and Peter Blumberg

item.title: Megadeals Defy Selloff, Head Toward Record
item.description: Wall Street is taking a big step toward a record year for mergers and acquisitions as some of the world’s largest companies defy a tech-induced selloff in global stocks to pursue major takeovers. Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu reports on "Bloomberg Deals." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Franklin Templeton's Araghi Sees AI Selloff as Market Reset
item.description: Franklin Templeton portfolio manager Sara Araghi says the sharp tech selloff reflects an unwinding of earlier AI euphoria rather than a fundamental deterioration in demand. She discusses why AI infrastructure spending remains strong, the growing focus on proving returns from that investment and why she still views Anthropic’s record IPO as a success despite shares falling below their offering price. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CoreWeave, Nvidia Credit Risk Hit Fresh Highs
item.description: Bloomberg's James Crombie joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." CoreWeave and Nvidia credit-risk measures hit fresh all-time highs Wednesday while gauges of perceived worry again reached levels last seen in March, as Wall Street grew increasingly concerned about the tech sector’s record borrowing to finance AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: S&P Says It May Downgrade Nvidia’s Ratings on Governance Worries
item.description: S&P Global Ratings is looking at cutting Nvidia Corp.’s credit by one notch, citing concerns over the company’s management and governance following the departure, and then the return, of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.
item.dc:creator: Davide Barbuscia

item.title: ElevenLabs in Early Talks for Funding at $33 Billion Value
item.description: ElevenLabs, a company building artificial intelligence voice models and agents, is in early discussions for a funding round at a target valuation of $33 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Tom Mackenzie, Yazhou Sun, Natasha Mascarenhas and Rebecca Torrence

item.title: SpaceX Wins Government Approval to Launch Space Data Centers
item.description: The US Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX’s request to launch as many as 1 million satellites for the creation of a network of data centers in orbit for complex artificial intelligence computing.
item.dc:creator: Sana Pashankar

item.title: Billions in Data Center Deals Grind to Halt After Chip Curbs
item.description: Lenders have hit the brakes on billions of dollars in loans tied to Chinese firms ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent, as new US curbs on chip access threaten to upend Asia’s burgeoning AI debt financing market.
item.dc:creator: Sheryl Tian Tong Lee, Kari Lindberg, Aileen Chuang and Megawati Wijaya
